content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text resolves C5 by individual verse bounds and almah/bethulah word-count rather than by chain-against-chain footing, so it does the thing K-C governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse — two readings weighed: (A) the collision must be resolved only by comparing the whole chains' footings; (B) the judge may resolve it by counting or balancing individual verses or words. I chose A as the rule's command.","why":"The judge's stated reasons treat the Isaiah 7:14 issue by individual verse bounds and almah/bethulah word-count, not by weighing chain against chain by footing, so it breaches K-C."}
